How a verified candidate moves to release

A mental model of the ownership boundary that keeps verification and publication attached to the same artifact.

The model in one sentence

Source creates a candidate once; verification describes that candidate; publication hands it off without reconstructing it.

Three ownership boundaries

  1. The builder returns an immutable path and identifier.
  2. Every gate reads that supplied candidate and records literal evidence.
  3. The publisher uploads the same path and adds the remote receipt.

Only three files own the path

  • src/release/candidate.ts
    Owns identity. Creates the candidate and returns its stable reference.
  • src/release/verify.ts
    Owns proof. Executes gates against the candidate it receives.
  • src/release/publish.ts
    Owns handoff. Uploads the verified reference and records external state.

A useful receipt carries identity

release-receipt.json
{
    "candidate": "archive-2026-07-25-01",
    "verified": ["focused-tests", "archive-inspection"],
    "published": "upload-receipt-4821"
  }

Two common category errors

Build is not runtime proof. A successful compile establishes source correctness only for that build context.

Remote green is not candidate identity. The check must name the artifact it evaluated.

Illustrative reference: replace all sample claims, dates, metrics, paths, and decisions with grounded source material.
